_schema_note: SR-31 (task-R9-brief.md fix round 1, review): measurements are a VERSIONED list under 'measurements.<version>', with 'active_measurement_version' selecting the live one. A re-measure (SR-2: Task C4, after dressing these worlds with prefab instances) adds a NEW version and bumps the selector -- it never edits a committed measurement's 'cameras'/'band'/'detects_total_deletion' fields in place, which is exactly the discipline the original (pre-fix-round) file's own prose asked for but could not enforce (band_for_world() read worlds.<name>.band directly, with no version selection at all, so the ONLY way to make a re-measurement take effect was the in-place edit the prose forbade).

1._provenance: S7a Task R9, REMEASURED at fix round 1 (SR-30/SR-31). measured: true. date: 2026-08-26. machine: DESKTOP-N7QJD3C (Windows 11, MSVC 19.44, msvc-ninja-release preset). worktree: C:/Users/ckbra/kat-wt/render-engine, branch spade/render, commit 4504440 (the original R9 landing) plus this fix round's own commit (this file's own values were produced by the code landing in the SAME commit that rewrites this file). limits_table_version: raymarch@SR-28 (kRaymarchMaxSteps=1024, kRaymarchSurfaceEpsilon=1e-4) plus tessellation@kTessellationDefaults@1 (unchanged since Task R3). resolution: 160x120. Every world is loaded straight from content/worlds/<name>.world.yaml via spade::load_world_file(), scene_from_world()'d with an EMPTY resolved-mesh span (no package instances, no props -- all ten are schema v1 and author none), and rendered with an explicitly-flattened sky. DrawMode::shaded has overlays=false and shadows=false. SR-30: every camera entry below carries 'probe_bare_ground_disagreement_fraction' -- the SAME real fast-path frame compared against a raymarch reference rendered from render::strip_to_ground_plane_only(world) (every SDF node deleted except the standalone ground-plane leaf) -- and 'detects_total_deletion', TRUE iff that probe value exceeds this camera's OWN 'band'. test_render_agreement.cpp's AgreementMatrix suite recomputes BOTH the real comparison and this probe LIVE on every run and asserts the live outcome matches 'detects_total_deletion' -- this field is a checked claim, not a narrated one. BAND RULE, uniform, no exceptions: band = round_up_to_nearest(0.001, max(0.001, 1.5 * disagreement_fraction)) -- per (world, camera), never per world (SR-30 point 3: a per-world band, using a world's max across its three cameras, LAUNDERED a discriminating camera's tight signal onto a non-discriminating one's inflated threshold -- see 'per_camera_banding_fix' below for the measured before/after). The floor of 0.001 exists only so a camera whose measured value is exactly 0.0 (every 'top_down' bookmark) still gets a small, non-zero regression tripwire rather than a hair-trigger zero. RE-MEASURE DISCIPLINE (SR-2, SR-31): Task C4 dressing these worlds with prefab instances adds a NEW entry under 'measurements' (e.g. version 2) and bumps 'active_measurement_version' -- this entry (version 1) stays exactly as measured, forever, as the audit trail of what bare-geometry agreement looked like before dressing.
1.per_camera_banding_fix: SR-30 point 3, with the number that motivated it: under the ORIGINAL per-WORLD banding (fix round 0), circuit-track's band was 0.025 -- the round-up of its OWN 'default' camera's 0.0166667, the world's own maximum across all three cameras. circuit-track/family_third's real committed disagreement was only 0.0076, so under per-world banding it inherited the SAME 0.025 band as 'default' -- but its OWN bare-ground probe measures 0.0174, comfortably UNDER 0.025 (no detection) despite being more than DOUBLE its own committed value. Moved to per-(world, camera) banding, family_third's OWN band (round_up(0.001, 1.5*0.0076) = 0.012) is correctly exceeded by that SAME 0.0174 probe -- circuit-track/family_third flips from 'does not detect' to 'detects' with the identical measured numbers, purely by removing the laundering. No other change was needed to fix this specific laundering; per-camera banding makes it structural rather than a rule to remember.
1.non_discriminating_summary: 23 of 30 cases have detects_total_deletion = false: all 10 'top_down' bookmarks (looking straight down puts no horizon, hence no sky, in frame at all -- both the real comparison and the bare-ground probe read exactly 0.0, always identical, structurally incapable of registering ANY reference geometry change under this coverage-vs-sky classifier), all 10 'default' bookmarks (the raster path also saturates -- or nearly saturates -- the frame with its own analytic ground, so the bare-ground probe is IDENTICAL or near-identical to the committed value on every one of them), and 3 of 10 'family_third' bookmarks (hover-pad, pdel-site, pfol-road -- see 'worlds_with_no_discriminating_camera' below). These 23 are not useless: they remain real tripwires against a change that breaks horizon-deficit saturation itself (SR-30 point 2), and 20 of them (all 'default'+'top_down') are also this program's real product camera bookmarks. But their band is, honestly, a horizon-deficit-and-noise band with a 1.5x multiplier -- it constrains no scene geometry today, and this field says so plainly rather than leaving that fact implicit in a table of numbers.
1.worlds_with_no_discriminating_camera: hover-pad, pdel-site and pfol-road each have ZERO discriminating cameras among their three bookmarks -- 'default' and 'top_down' behave as documented above (non-discriminating everywhere), and their 'family_third' ALSO does not discriminate: hover-pad's and pdel-site's bare-ground probes are BIT-IDENTICAL to their committed real values (0.00833333 and 0.0105208 respectively, to the printed digit), and pfol-road's probe (0.00833333) is even slightly BELOW its committed value (0.00875). The likely cause (a finding, not a fix -- this belongs to Task C4, which owns these bookmarks per the controller's own instruction): all three worlds' non-ground geometry near this camera is low-relief relative to the ground plane at this resolution and viewing angle (hover-pad's own pad, e.g., is a 0.05 m-tall cylinder against a 3 m camera distance) -- thin enough that deleting it changes no pixel's coverage classification at 160x120. Task C4 should read this before assuming these three worlds' agreement bands say anything about their actual geometry: today, none of their three shipped bookmarks do.
1.heightfield_forward_note_for_phase_3: Forwarded per the task brief's own instruction ('whoever does that needs to know this exists'): SR-17's analytic-ground device (render/scene.hpp's GroundPlane list) covers a standalone 'prim: plane' node ONLY. None of today's ten shipped worlds uses a 'prim: heightfield' ground (confirmed: grep -n \"prim: heightfield\" across all ten content/worlds/*.world.yaml returns nothing -- every apparent hit is a params-legend COMMENT line, not a real node), so this gap is LATENT, not live, in the current corpus. Task R8's own measurement on the spade test corpus's maximal.world.yaml (a heightfield-grounded world, NOT one of the ten shipped worlds) found a >100% relative disagreement from exactly this gap -- twenty times this task's own >5%-is-a-real-bug gate. Phase 3 content tasks C1-C4: if a heightfield ground is introduced to any shipped world, expect a large, genuine disagreement here that is a real SR-17 gap, not a band to widen -- either extend SR-17's analytic ground to cover heightfield, or exclude heightfield-grounded worlds from this matrix with the SAME honesty this file applies to its own non-discriminating cases above.
1.thin_margin_note: Every detecting case is described by margin_over_band = probe_bare_ground_disagreement_fraction / band (added fix round 2, review finding: record thin margins beside the bands, not just the pass/fail outcome). Two of the seven detecting cases clear their own band by less than 1.3x under TOTAL deletion, the most extreme mutation this probe can apply: swarm-grid/family_third at 1.1545x and pint-box/family_third at 1.278x. A future re-derivation of the band rule (the 1.5x-and-round-up multiplier, or the round-up step itself) that widens bands by more than roughly 15-20% would silently move these two out of the detecting set (7 of 30) into the non-discriminating one (23 of 30) with nothing to notice unless this field is read and re-checked at that time. The other five detecting cases have comfortable margins (1.45x to 138x) and are not at similar risk from a modest band-rule change.

2.props_do_not_perturb_this_matrix: Task C4 (SR-54) placed real props (mesh-based, render-only) in 9 of the ten worlds for the first time -- verified here, not assumed: every one of this measurement's 30 real disagreement_fraction/covered_a/covered_b values is either BIT-IDENTICAL to measurement 1's bare-geometry value (23 of 30 cases) or differs only by the SDF prefab instances also added in the same recipe edit (the remaining 7 family_third cases, where covered_a moved by the same handful of pixels a new mast/barrier/fence contributes). No case shows a change attributable to a prop, because none can, by construction: this suite's own scene_or_fail() (test_render_agreement.cpp) always calls scene_from_world() with an EMPTY resolved-mesh span, so every prop's mesh_ref misses that span's lookup and resolves to kNoMesh (render/scene.cpp:340-352), skipped identically on the path that would draw it -- the SAME fact is true whether the harness sees 0 props (measurement 1) or dozens (measurement 2). The honest conclusion, stated plainly rather than left implicit: this matrix does not validate props at all, in either measurement. C5's gallery is where props get checked, by eye.

This is evidence against a live defect at today's camera framings, not proof the grid margin is safe in general: most of the ten worlds' three bookmarks do not frame either prefab's thin features close-up (see task-C4-report.md's T6 section for the honest scope of what was and was not actually exercised).

pdel-site.family_third.why: The original bookmark targeted the aerial 'start' spawn point itself (an empty point in space, 8m from every piece of dressed geometry) -- measured, before AND after dressing, as bit-identical bare-ground noise (0.0105208 both times), proving the hangar-shell/platform Task C4 added there were never in this camera's frustum at all. Re-framed to a 3/4 elevated side view of the new hangar-shell (target = its centre, viewed from its +X side) -- still a third-person-over-the-action framing (RS9/CS5's own purpose for this bookmark), now over the site's actual dressed structure instead of an empty point. Two earlier re-frame attempts (aimed through the hangar's own doorway opening, and from directly behind it) measured as non-discriminating too (0.00833/0.0167 real disagreement, probe bit-identical to real) before this one worked -- kept here as the honest record that this took iteration, not a single correct guess.
